The effort field MEASURES what US2 AS2 (report names the tiers that ran), AS3 (one fixed effort for ad-hoc judges) and AS4 (the run log records each session's effort) ask; enforcement of the request, not scope. decisions.summary: Claims file: the page-session rules say only how the file is read and written, so what blocks a run is the brief's to say; the write brief now says feature-293 lines the run did not write are not claims on its work (identical in both arms); the launcher's release line stays as a record; no per-run copy
decisions.why: The purpose of D5 is that the second R run is not blocked by the first run's claim, so both arms start from the same effective state; an identical instruction in both briefs does that, D6 still records the claims file as each run found it (the shared-resource edge case), and the per-run copy was only the fallback for the rules not honoring a release. The WORDING of the sentence is a separate decision (prompt-names-effort).

decisions.summary: prompts/R-write.md (claims line and the T08 sentence) and prompts/R-check.md line 33 tell the run it is in an 'Effort experiment' and that another run of the same task exists whose output is set aside; every prompt (R-write, R-check, I) also points the run's handoff files into specs/293-effort-level-experiment/
decisions.why: FR-004: the prompt gives the task, the future-work location, the stop point, the no-human-help rule, 'and nothing about effort'. A prompt that tells a session it is a subject of an effort experiment is about effort, and the handoff's 'byte-identical task prompt' control is there so that the only thing acting on the run is its effort level. Nothing makes this impossible: the claims label can be '293 | task R ...' and the sentence 'lines for 293 that you did not write are not claims on your work'; the handoff files can be written under a neutral path in the clone. Symmetry across arms is not a defense - FR-004 is a separate clause from 'identical across arms'. The prompts are drafts not yet frozen, so the fix costs minutes.
